build(bk7258): make the daily build/package/flash loop need no paths
Packaging created a fresh timestamped directory on every run, so flashing meant
copying a path out of the packager's output, and picking the newest of fifteen
similar directories by eye. build.sh already avoids that: it derives its binary
directory from the config as <board>_<config>, so configs/cp lands in
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp with no -b at all. The wrappers now match that.

bk7258-package.sh writes cmake_out/bk7258-l2-bundled and replaces what was there,
and bk7258-flash.sh defaults to the same directory, so the loop is four commands
with no arguments and the image flashed is always the one just built. Replacing a
package also removes any loader log left from flashing the older image, so a stale
log can never be read as evidence for a new one.

Keeping a run as evidence stays possible and is now the explicit case: name it
with --output-dir and it is never replaced unless --overwrite is given too, since
an image that produced a UART log has to stay exactly as it was flashed.

The regression test gains two checks. One compares the wrappers' default paths
against build.sh's own derivation rule, because a mismatch there would silently
flash a stale image rather than fail. The other exercises the wrapper end to end:
the scratch directory must be repackageable, a named one must refuse to be
replaced for that reason and not merely exit non-zero, and an overwrite must not
leave a stale loader log behind. expect_failure() can now assert why a command
failed, so a typo in an invocation no longer passes as a rejection.

build(bk7258): take the linker RAM window from Kconfig, guard cross-domain RAM
flash.ld hard-coded the same RAM window that configs/cp already declares as
CONFIG_RAM_START/CONFIG_RAM_SIZE, so one fact lived in two places with nothing
but habit keeping them equal. The script now includes nuttx/config.h and takes
the window from Kconfig, which is what 94 linker scripts in tree already do and
what the AP script will need in order to describe a different window without
diverging in shape.

Flash stays literal: CONFIG_FLASH_START/CONFIG_FLASH_SIZE are 0 here, and the
vector base is already cross-checked against the packaging profile by the L1
validator.

The chip header cannot be used from a linker script -- it pulls in stdint.h and
UINT32_C() suffixes that the linker rejects -- so the cross-domain guard lives in
bk7258_allocateheap.c instead, beside the code computing the heap's upper bound.
Two static_asserts now fail the build if a component's RAM window leaves the SoC
SRAM or reaches into PWR_MNG/SWAP. Without them, a component growing over the
fixed-address CP/AP ABI would silently corrupt the other domain instead of
failing to link.

Verified both directions: configs/cp still yields a byte-identical app.bin with
unchanged sections and symbol table, the preprocessed MEMORY block expands to the
same addresses, and raising CONFIG_RAM_SIZE past PWR_MNG fails the build with the
overlap assertion rather than producing an image.

refactor(bk7258): bound the heap with CONFIG_RAM_END, add SoC memory anchors
BK7258_SRAM_BASE/SIZE/END named themselves after the chip but held the CP
carveout, so anyone reading them literally once AP exists would have aimed at
AP_RAM. They also duplicated CONFIG_RAM_START/CONFIG_RAM_SIZE by hand, giving
two places to keep in sync for one fact.

up_allocate_heap() now bounds the heap with CONFIG_RAM_END, as 20 arch heap
allocators in tree already do. It is derived from each component's own
CONFIG_RAM_START/CONFIG_RAM_SIZE, so CP and AP each get their configured window
with nothing to synchronise, and the three macros are deleted rather than
renamed -- the drift source is removed, not relabelled.

In their place the chip header carries what is genuinely chip-level: the whole
SRAM window, and the fixed-address cross-domain regions AP_SPINLOCK, PWR_MNG and
SWAP that neither image may cover with .data, .bss, a stack or a heap. How the
window is split between CP and AP stays a board decision, so no CP or AP
carveout is declared here.

Values follow the vendor layout and are semantic anchors for the AP work, not a
frozen contract; the AP_RAM / RPMSG_SHM split still has to be measured against

onward, so it belongs to configs/cp as a switch flipped at that point. If an
explicit toggle turns out to be useful, the board convention is a single
aggregating symbol that selects RPTUN and RPMSG_UART, not a copied defconfig.

Also drop the provisional rpmsg_serialinit() hook. It carried an unverified
placeholder cpuname, and uart_rpmsg only binds when that name matches the remote
exactly, so leaving it in place would have looked functional while never linking.
It returns in A2 together with the real cpuname and rptun_ops_s.

The footprint numbers this scaffolding produced are recorded in the research
document instead: the stack costs about 56 KiB flash at the upper bound and
about 13 KiB heap, so RPTUN does not force CP_RAM to shrink and only the shared
carveout needs reserving.

Verified: configs/cp builds clean and app.bin is byte-identical to the baseline.

---
7e0af8f853e4f8299c5b1f98b88130f5a20b3638
chenzepei3 <chenzepei3@xiaomi.com>
build(bk7258): follow the upstream post-build convention for L1 export
Restructure the L1 export/validation to match how boards in tree actually do
post-build work: a nuttx_post_build custom target plus
add_custom_command(TARGET ... POST_BUILD), as used by rp2040, spresense and sim.
No board in tree uses add_custom_command(OUTPUT ...) for this, and none names a
generated file as a file-level dependency.

That distinction is what made the previous form fragile: dependencies are now
expressed on targets only, and link side effects such as nuttx.map are declared
through BYPRODUCTS instead of being named as prerequisites. Ordering comes from
the framework, which wires nuttx_post_build after nuttx_post.

Verified against a pre-change build of configs/cp: app.bin is byte-identical,
.text/.data/.bss and the whole symbol table are unchanged, and the L1 validator
still reports pass.

---
92d504ba82caa17ed2d53f47879d726377b392c7
chenzepei3 <chenzepei3@xiaomi.com>
docs(bk7258-ap): correct AP lifecycle and console command references
Three corrections found while verifying the plan against the tree:

BOARDIOC_START_CPU already exists and board.h documents it as starting a slave
core "under the pseudo AMP case which is different with armv7-a/armv8-a SMP" --
exactly CP releasing CPU1. Route A0 through board_start_cpu() instead of
inventing a private start API, and let rptun_ops.start call the same hook from
A2 so there is only one release path. Query/reset/stop and boot-record dump have
no standard interface, so those stay a board-local builtin.

CONFIG_BOARDCTL is already enabled indirectly: CONFIG_NSH_ARCHINIT selects it,
and board_app_initialize() already exists. A0 only needs
CONFIG_BOARDCTL_START_CPU.

The console forwarder is apps/system/cu ("cu -l /dev/ttyAP", "~." to hang up),
not a command named cuterm and not something we need to write ourselves.

---
15ed9a675a6855932658668fc74a07d0f26e7adf
chenzepei3 <chenzepei3@xiaomi.com>
build(bk7258): add cp_rptun measurement config and rpmsg_serialinit hook
Add a configs/cp_rptun variant that enables RPTUN/RPMsg/OpenAMP on CP, so the
footprint of that stack can be measured before the CP_RAM/AP_RAM/SWAP split is
frozen. Following the Vela convention of parallel config directories
(nsh_cm7 / nsh_cm7_rptun), building configs/cp returns to the plain CP NSH
image, so the measurement carries its own revert path.

drivers_initialize() references rpmsg_serialinit() unconditionally under
CONFIG_RPMSG_UART, so the board must define it. Keep it as a real
uart_rpmsg_init() call rather than an empty stub: with --gc-sections and archive
linking an empty stub drops uart_rpmsg.c from the image entirely and any
footprint measured that way is meaningless. The cpuname is a placeholder and
isconsole stays false, since UART0 already owns CP's /dev/console.

Verified that the guarded block has no effect on configs/cp: bk7258_bringup.c.o
is identical in size and sections with and without this change.

---
81f556cb6d08472dad1a573867d0128b43fcff8f
chenzepei3 <chenzepei3@xiaomi.com>
fix(bk7258): keep nuttx.map out of DEPENDS so clean builds work
nuttx.map is only a side effect of the link step: the arch layer appends
-Wl,-Map=nuttx.map under CONFIG_DEBUG_LINK_MAP and no CMake rule ever declares
that file as an OUTPUT or BYPRODUCTS. Listing it in DEPENDS made ninja reject
the entire graph with "missing and no known rule to make it", so a clean build
failed and only a tree carrying a stale map from an earlier link appeared to
work. Ordering already comes from nuttx_post, which depends on the nuttx link.

Also gate the map export on CONFIG_DEBUG_LINK_MAP so turning the option off
does not break the copy step, and let the validator depend on the exported
artifact list instead of the raw build-directory path.

---
d65ef3e08e83fb396acb2c28cf890f94aed0ede1
chenzepei3 <chenzepei3@xiaomi.com>
docs(bk7258-ap): record AP multicore research and bring-up evidence chain
Freeze the source-backed model behind AP bring-up so the implementation does
not re-litigate it: Armino runs CP/AP as AMP with an SMP pair inside the single
AP image, its console is a CP UART0 aggregator reached per-command through
ap_cmd over Mailbox, and BK7258 Mailbox is a notification device while the
shared SRAM layout stays entirely under software control.

Also record the evidence rule that blocks premature completion claims:
building and packaging app1.bin proves nothing by itself, so every stage
carries one piece of evidence that does not depend on the next stage.
